item.title: Intermediate subalgebras of cross-product von Neumann algebras arising from weakly compact actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.33320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short paper, we establish the following Galois-type property for all measure-preserving, weakly compact actions $G \curvearrowright (X,\mu) $ of a non-inner amenable group $G$ on a standard probability space $X$: for any intermediate von Neumann subalgebra $\mathcal L(G)\subseteq \mathcal N \subseteq L^\infty (X)\rtimes G$, there is a factor $G\curvearrowright Y$ of $G \curvearrowright X$ such that $\mathcal N= L^\infty(Y)\rtimes G$. In particular, this holds for all pmp distal actions $G\curvearrowright X$, thereby answering positively an open problem from \cite{BCCMSW24} (which can also be traced back to \cite{CD20}). We also provide an example showing our result is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Ionut Chifan, Zachary Flood

item.title: Sharp Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.33686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp $2$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroups with $-1<q<1$ and obtain hypercontractivity along the Gross curve with the optimal coefficient, and determine the exact hypercontractive time for $1<p\le2\le r<\infty$. Reverse hypercontractivity holds in the two separate ranges $0<p<r<1$ and $-\infty<p<r<0$. An explicit counterexample rules out the proposed universal reverse curve across zero. We also obtain the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality via the intertwining property.
item.dc:creator: Jinsong Wu

item.title: Regularity and selfless cp maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.34000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the regularity properties of C*-algebras admitting a weakly selfless unital completely positive map.
item.dc:creator: Miles Gould, Leonel Robert

item.title: Operator systems in \'etale groupoid C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study operator systems arising from positivity domains of \'etale groupoids with compact unit space. Extending Kavruk's enough unitaries principle we show that such operator systems are hyperrigid in the C$^*$-algebra they generate. We focus on operator systems of positivity domains in UHF algebras and, by identifying them with Cantor graph operator systems, we show that they are hyperrigid. Furthermore, we show that in general, such a characterization is not possible when the \'etaleness condition of the underlying groupoid is removed, due to the failure of reduced spectral and compact operator synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Georgios Baziotis, Douglas Farenick, Evgenios T. A. Kakariadis, Malte Leimbach, Lyudmila Turowska, Walter D. van Suijlekom

item.title: How characterisations of traces and central elements fail: sharp violation constants via michelson contrast and noncentrality
item.description: arXiv:2610.34388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A positive functional is a trace if and only if it satisfies any one of many inequalities, the first being Gardner's $|\varphi(X)|\le\varphi(|X|)$; positive central elements are characterised similarly. We ask how strongly these characterisations fail. For $\varphi=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,\cdot)$ on a matrix algebra the natural scale is the Michelson contrast $\delta$ of the density. For Gardner's inequality the sharp constant depends on $\delta$ and on the contrast $\delta'$ of $|X|$ only through their product: it is $(1-\delta^2\delta'^2)^{-1/2}$, the secant of the angle whose sine is $\delta\delta'$. On a finite von Neumann algebra the contrast is the wrong parameter, since every central density gives a trace; the governing parameter is the noncentrality, defined through the central condition number $\kappa_Z(\rho)$ of the central envelopes of $\rho$ (the largest and smallest elements of Halpern's central spectrum). A transfer principle lifts sharp matrix constants to exact constants in terms of $\kappa_Z$ in every finite von Neumann algebra. For 38 trace characterisations the constant is exact in 23 cases, has proved bounds in 13 and is known only numerically in two; for instance it is $\cosh(\frac12\ln\kappa_Z)$ for Gardner's inequality and for the subadditivity of the modulus. On matrix algebras the finite exact violations vanish at the trace to the orders $\delta$, $\delta^2$ or $\delta^4$, and outside factors and abelian algebras no function of the contrast describes the constants. We also find the sharp constants of the Novikov-Tikhonov characterisations of central elements, sharp bounds for three unnormalised trace functionals, and sharp contrast thresholds below which subadditivity of the square root and the power-mean inequality cannot fail. A numerical search, certified as a lower bound for each supremum, supports conjectured values for the remaining inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Sami Abdullah Abed, Irina Nikolaeva, Andrej Novikov

item.title: Local Reflexivity and Exactness for Reduced $C^*$-Algebras of Wreath Products
item.description: arXiv:2610.34695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every countable non-exact discrete group $H$ and every nontrivial countable discrete group $K$, the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is not locally reflexive. These provide the first known examples of non-locally reflexive reduced group $C^*$-algebras, settling a longstanding existence question. Moreover, for every nontrivial countable exact discrete group $K$, we establish that local reflexivity of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$ is equivalent to exactness of $H$, and hence to exactness of $C_r^*(K\wr H)$. This gives a partial affirmative answer to Kirchberg's question of whether local reflexivity implies exactness for $C^*$-algebras. As applications, we construct finitely generated groups with the Haagerup property, as well as finitely generated residually finite groups, whose reduced group $C^*$-algebras are not locally reflexive. In particular, neither the Haagerup property nor coarse embeddability into Hilbert space guarantees local reflexivity of the associated reduced group $C^*$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Pingchuan Dong, Zhe Dong

item.title: Measure Convergence under Weak Domination for Unitarily Invariant Norms on Finite von Neumann Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem (DCT) is a cornerstone in commutative measure theory, while its extension to the noncommutative setting has remained a longstanding challenge due to the barriers posed by the noncommutative structure. Let \(\alpha\) be a unitarily invariant norm defined on a diffuse tracial von Neumann algebra \((\mathcal{M}, \tau)\), let $L^\alpha(\mathcal M, \tau)$ be the completion of $\mathcal M$ with respect to the norm $\alpha$(which includes all $L^p(\mathcal M, \tau)$ as special cases). In this paper, by replacing ``almost everywhere convergence" with Nelson's convergence in measure, we establish a noncommutative analog of the dominated convergence theorem for $L^\alpha(\mathcal M, \tau)$ under a { significantly weaker dominating condition} than those previously considered. For instance, in a \(II_1\) factor \(\mathcal{M}\), if \(P\) is a projection with \(\tau(P)=\frac{1}{n}\), then \(n^2 P\) ``dominates" every operator of norm \(\leq n\). As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of center-preserving $*$-automorphism of finite von Neumann algebras, which unifies and extends the earlier works of Kadison and Haagerup on the structure of automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Yanni Chen, Don Hadwin, Junhao Shen, Ye Zhang

item.title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.35290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.
item.dc:creator: Antonio M. Peralta, Pedro Saavedra

item.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $\sigma$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,\sigma)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action $\alpha$ satisfies that $\overline{\alpha(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,\sigma)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $\alpha$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $\alpha:G\curvearrowright (D,\sigma)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action with $\overline{\alpha(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Toyota

item.title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
item.description: arXiv:2610.35674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Guoliang Yu

item.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
item.description: arXiv:2610.35774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a weight on a C$^*$-algebra is lower semi-continuous if it is lower semi-continuous on commutative C$^*$-subalgebras. This can be used to prove a von Neumann algebraic counterpart that a weight on a von Neumann algebra is normal if it is normal on commutative von Neumann subalgebras. This provides an affirmative solution to Haagerup's second problem (Problem 1.11) on normal weights posed in 1975.
item.dc:creator: David P. Blecher, Ikhan Choi

item.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.
item.dc:creator: Eusebio Gardella, Tabar\'e Roland

item.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.
item.dc:creator: Cathy Cheng, Nigel Higson, Danilo Polo Ojito, Emil Prodan

item.title: Orthograph related to mutual (strong) numerical radius orthogonality on operator algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.33422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{B} (H)$ and $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{B} (H)$, respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on $\mathcal{B} (H)$ or $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Shaoxing Sun, Jinchuan Hou, Xiaofei Qi

item.title: Weakly Unitary Zeon Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.33891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, zeon matrix groups are discussed for the first time. Extending the concept of unitary complex matrices (i.e., matrices $A$ such that $A^\dagger A=\mI$) to matrices having entries in the complex zeon algebra $\CZ$, a ``zeon dagger'' operator $\zdag$ is defined and used to declare a zeon matrix $\Xi$ to be {\em unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI$. The unitary zeon matrices of order $n$ form a subgroup $\U_n$ of all invertible order-$n$ zeon matrices. A more interesting notion is that of ``weak unitarity'' of a zeon matrix. In particular, a zeon matrix $\Xi$ will be said to be {\em weakly unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI+\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a diagonal nilpotent zeon matrix. The weakly unitary matrices of order $n$ form a group $\W_n$, of which $\U_n$ is a subgroup. It is further shown that the exponential of a graph's nilpotent adjacency matrix has a natural orthogonal decomposition into the sum of a weakly unitary zeon matrix and a nilpotent zeon matrix. Eigenvalues of the weakly unitary zeon matrix reveal information about the graph's cycles and paths.
item.dc:creator: G. Stacey Staples

item.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Hao Guo, Chenxi Wang, Guoliang Yu

item.title: Word Trace Formulas over Compact Groups and Connected Cumulants
item.description: arXiv:2610.34213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the expected value of the product of traces for a finite set of words within any compact subgroup of $\mathcal(N)$. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition under which these values determine that the product of the conjugacy classes of the words contains the identity.
item.dc:creator: Liviu Paunescu, Florin Radulescu

item.title: A Reduction Bound for Entanglement Detection by Positive Free Maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.34338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collins, Hayden, and Nechita used free probability to construct families of $k$-positive but not $(k+1)$-positive maps and applied them to entanglement detection. We prove that positive free maps associated with compactly supported freely infinitely divisible distributions are no stronger than the reduction criterion in every ancillary dimension. In particular, these maps cannot detect positive partial transpose entanglement. The proof combines a joint Fock realization with an operator positivity certificate derived from free L\'evy data.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yen Lee

item.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
item.dc:creator: Li Gao, Lijun Wang

item.title: $\mathcal{W}$-absorbing actions of finite groups on the Razak-Jacelon algebra
item.description: arXiv:2410.11213v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We say that a countable discrete group action $\alpha$ on a C$^*$-algebra $A$ is \textit{$\mathcal{W}$-absorbing} if there exist a C$^*$-algebra $B$ and an action $\beta$ on $B$ such that $\alpha$ is cocycle conjugate to $\beta\otimes \mathrm{id}_{\mathcal{W}}$ on $B\otimes \mathcal{W}$ where $\mathcal{W}$ is the Razak-Jacelon algebra. In this paper, we completely classify outer $\mathcal{W}$-absorbing actions of finite groups on $\mathcal{W}$ up to conjugacy and cocycle conjugacy.
item.dc:creator: Norio Nawata

item.title: $T$-admissible processes and noncommutative weighted ergodic theorems
item.description: arXiv:2604.26224v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the bilaterally almost uniform (b.a.u.) convergence of weighted averages of a positive Dunford-Schwartz operator $T$ acting on the noncommutative $L_p$-spaces $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ associated to a semifinite von Neumann algebra $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$ for a variety of sequences which includes those generated by bounded i.i.d. sequences, the M\"{o}bius function, the Liouville function, and totally balanced automatic sequences. If $1<p<\infty$, then sequences generated by i.i.d. sequences with finite $q$-th moment for $q=\frac{p}{p-1}$ being the H\"{o}lder conjugate of $p$ are also shown to generate good weights for $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We also study similar problems for $T$-admissible processes on a semifinite von Neumann algebra, showing that if a Wiener-Wintner type ergodic theorem holds for a class $\mathcal{W}\subset W_q$ of weights, then it also holds for strongly $p$-bounded $T$-admissible processes assuming that the duality $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$ holds and that $T$ is a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism. A version of this result for arbitrary positive Dunford-Schwartz operators is also considered.
item.dc:creator: Morgan O'Brien

item.title: Functional Calculus on Noncommutative Tori, II. Complex Powers, Logarithms, and Sectorial Projections
item.description: arXiv:2607.17516v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a systematic theory of complex powers, logarithms, and sectorial projections of elliptic pseudodifferential operators on noncommutative tori, extending to this setting the classical constructions of Seeley and others. Building on the parametric pseudodifferential calculus of the prequel~\cite{LP:Part1}, we construct the complex powers associated with a given ray, show that they form a holomorphic family of pseudodifferential operators with the semigroup property, and compute their symbols. We further establish exponential growth bounds on vertical strips in the operator, Schatten, and trace-class topologies by means of a new holomorphic calculus for pseudodifferential families. The logarithm is identified as a pseudodifferential operator whose symbol is determined by the resolvent symbol, and the associated trace formula is derived. Sectorial projections are constructed as contour integrals and shown to be of order zero. This yields analogues for noncommutative tori of results of Wodzicki, Okikiolu, and Gaarde--Grubb, and provides the analytic foundations for the spectral-geometric applications developed in subsequent papers.
item.dc:creator: Gihyun Lee, Raphael Ponge

item.title: Maximal Algebraic Ideals in Nonunital $C^*$-Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.18840v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of maximal algebraic two-sided ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras. We formulate singular-distribution estimates in terms of lower semicontinuous $2$-quasitraces and introduce a novel criterion, which we call an admissible compact quasitracial triple set. These tools allow us to control membership in algebraic ideals and to prove the nonexistence of maximal ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras under a closed finite-scale face condition. This nonexistence result applies to a broad class of simple $C^*$-algebras including simple separable stable AF algebras, and nonunital, simple, separable, stably finite, $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras $A$ that admit an approximate identity consisting of increasing projections $(p_n)$ and for which the simplex $\operatorname{QT}_2^1(A,p_1)$ of normalized traces at $p_1$ has finitely many extreme points. Moreover, we construct a simple AF algebra whose finite-scale face is dense but not closed and which nevertheless has a maximal dense algebraic ideal. This example yields a negative resolution to a question raised by Ozawa, asking whether every maximal algebraic two-sided ideal in a $C^*$-algebra must be closed.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Liu, Xin Ma

item.title: $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless inclusions for the infinite braid group
item.description: arXiv:2609.38596v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $B_\infty$ be the braid group on infinitely many strands and $P_\infty$ its pure braid group. We show that $C^*_r(P_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ and all its intermediate inclusions are $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and completely selfless. This gives natural examples of simple nonnuclear $\mathcal{Z}$-stable $C^*$-algebras. Further examples come from $\mathrm{SL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_\infty(\mathbb{Z})$. We also show that $C^*_r(\mathbb{F}_\infty)\subseteq C^*_r(B_\infty)$ is completely selfless for the free group $\mathbb{F}_\infty$ of braids in which only the first strand moves. All results hold for twisted group $C^*$-algebras. In contrast, $\mathcal{Z}$-stability fails for $B_n$ with $n$ finite and for groups that are not inner amenable.
item.dc:creator: Tron Omland

item.title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2305.01499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.
item.dc:creator: K. Mahesh Krishna

item.title: Fej\'er--Riesz factorization for positive noncommutative trigonometric polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2511.09267v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a Fej\'er-Riesz type factorization for positive matrix-valued noncommutative trigonometric polynomials on $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, where $\mathscr{W}$ is either the free semigroup $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{g}$, and $\mathfrak{Y}$ is a discrete group. More precisely, using the shortlex order, if $A$ has degree at most $w$ in the $\mathscr{W}$ variables and is uniformly strictly positive on all unitary representations of $\mathscr{W}\times\mathfrak{Y}$, then $A=B^{*}B$ with $B$ analytic and of $\mathscr{W}$-degree at most $w$; this degree bound is optimal, and strict positivity is essential. As an application, we obtain degree-bounded sums-of-squares certificates for Bell-type inequalities in $\mathbb{C}[\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}\times \mathbb{Z}_2^{*h}]$ from quantum information theory. In the special case $\mathscr{W}=\mathbb{Z}^h$ we recover, in the matrix-valued setting, the classical commutative multivariable Fej\'er-Riesz factorization. For trivial $\mathfrak{Y}$ we obtain a ``perfect'' group-algebra Positivstellensatz on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ that does not require strict positivity; this result is sharp, as demonstrated by counterexamples in $\mathbb{Z}_2*\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_3^{*2}$. To establish our main results two novel ingredients of independent interest are developed: (a) a positive-semidefinite Parrott theorem with entries given by functions on a group; and (b) solutions to positive semidefinite matrix completion problems for $\langle x \rangle_g$ or the free product group $\mathbb{Z}_2^{*g}$ indexed by words in $\mathscr{W}$ of length $\le w$.
item.dc:creator: Igor Klep, Jacob Levenson, Scott McCullough

item.title: Teleportation=Translation: Continuous recovery of black hole information
item.description: arXiv:2512.11877v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The \textit{Teleportation=Translation} conjecture posits that the recovery of information from a black hole is dual to a geometric translation in the emergent spacetime. In this paper, we establish this equivalence for general local quantum field theories by constructing a continuous unitary interpolation that bridges discrete algebraic teleportation protocols and continuous modular flow. We resolve the failure of dynamic idempotency, fundamentally inherent in Type III von Neumann algebras, by employing the Haagerup-Kosaki crossed-product construction. This lift to the semifinite Type~II$_\infty$ envelope yields a canonical, dynamically consistent path. Crucially, we prove that its unique infinitesimal generator $\tilde{G}$ is exactly twice the geometric modular momentum ($\tilde{G}=2P$). We establish this identity as a closed operator equivalence using Nelson's analytic vector theorem and quantify its structural robustness via non-commutative $L^p$ theory. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unitary information recovery fundamentally manifests as a continuous geometric translation. This provides a rigorous operator-algebraic mechanism for resolving the black hole information paradox, offering a kinematic framework naturally extendable to include gravitational back-reaction.
item.dc:creator: Jeongwon Ho

item.title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
item.description: arXiv:2608.19286v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\lambda P_\lambda$, where $\Lambda\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}P_\lambda=I$ in the strong operator topology. We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$. We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.
item.dc:creator: Nag Puspendu, Golla Ramesh

item.title: Spectral gap, internality of relative commutants, and non-hyperlinear groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.37761v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the relative commutant of a finite unitary tuple in a tracial matrix ultraproduct is internal whenever its conjugation operator has a spectral gap off the commutant. This implies the existence of a non-hyperlinear group.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Alekseev, Jihao Liu, Andreas Thom
